title: a text hit on a whiteboard file renders twice, once by path and once by node moniker
body:
`intent search "expired snapshot" --limit 8` renders each hit on a whiteboard file twice: once with the path in the second column and once with the node's moniker (`intent/whiteboard/cc/.history/20260815/inbox.vc.md:1987  file  intent/whiteboard/cc/.history/20260815/inbox.vc.md  ...` then the same line with `cc`; likewise `vc`, `ic`). Eight rows shown carry four distinct hits. Either the two rows are two records for one line (a file hit and a board hit) and one of them should not be a `file`, or the renderer prints one record twice. The `.history` archives dominating a text search's top rows is a separate question about the prose corpus, not filed here.

Addendum: the JSON for `intent search "expired snapshot" --limit 3 --json` carries the whiteboard hit twice with identical fields (kind `file`, the same name, path, line and snippet), so the doubling is two records in the answer, not the prose renderer printing one record twice.

CLOSED 2026-09-14 (dc): a path indexed before the store came to carry it (a board `.history` snapshot, after rule 0304) was never removed by a refresh, because `changed_under` removed only paths gone from disk; its `file` rows stayed beside the snapshot's `wb_node` sections. A previously indexed path that is now carried is removed too. Before (live store, read-only): the `.history` hit at line 1987 appeared twice, owners the path and `cc`. After (a read-only `.backup` copy of the live store, one whole-scope reconcile with the fixed build): file-owned `.history` sections 6953 -> 7, wb_node sections 6952 unchanged, and each `.history` hit answers once (`cc` 1987, `vc` 145, `ic` 43, `vc` 37). The 7 left are `.history` files the store does not carry as snapshots, so they have one owner.
